item.text:
**3B.1 Note**
Xi Jinping’s 2024 record is overwhelmingly negative on protection from state violence and coercive detention. The only meaningful counterevidence I found is narrow: one Tibet-specific finding of no known arbitrary/unlawful killings that year, plus a few isolated Hong Kong due-process outcomes. Those do not offset the broader pattern of torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, and impunity.

| Assessment | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Partial/limited positive | `2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: China (Includes Hong Kong, Macau, and Tibet)—Tibet` | U.S. Department of State | 2025-08-12 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128584.html | For Tibet in 2024, the report says there were no known reports or credible allegations of arbitrary or unlawful killings. This is the strongest narrow positive item I found, but it is limited to killings in one region and does not show broad protection from detention, torture, or disappearance. | `3B.1` |
| Partial/limited positive | `Hong Kong's landmark national security trial for 47 democrats` | Reuters | 2024-05-30 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hong-kongs-landmark-national-security-trial-for-47-democrats-3462427 | In the Hong Kong 47 case, four activists were released on bail after prosecutors withdrew an appeal, and two defendants were acquitted. This shows small pockets of procedure, but the broader case still involved mass political prosecution and detention. | `3B.1` |
| Strong negative | `2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: China` | U.S. Department of State | 2025-08-12 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128572.html | The report says China had credible reports of arbitrary/unlawful killings, disappearances, torture, and arbitrary detention, including more than one million Uyghurs held in extrajudicial internment camps or prisons; it also cites the torture death of Sun Renze and says the government took no credible steps to punish abusers. | `3B.1` |
| Strong negative | `World Report 2025: China` | Human Rights Watch | 2025-01-?? | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/china | HRW says about half a million Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims remained imprisoned, with no mass releases, and that Xi visited Xinjiang and called his policies there a “success” despite the UN’s prior findings of arbitrary arrests, torture, and enforced disappearances. | `3B.1` |
| Strong negative | `Hong Kong 47`: Court wraps up mitigation hearing in city’s largest national security case | Reuters | 2024-09-03 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hong-kong-47-court-wraps-up-mitigation-hearing-in-citys-largest-national-security-case-2250280 | Reuters reported that 47 activists were prosecuted under the Beijing-imposed national security law, with 32 initially denied bail and the rest kept in custody under strict conditions. This is direct evidence of political imprisonment and exemplary punishment. | `3B.1` |
| Strong negative | `China: Activist Li Qiaochu unjustly convicted ‘for speaking out about torture’` | Amnesty International | 2024-02-05 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/china-activist-li-qiaochu-unjustly-convicted-for-speaking-out-about-torture/ | Amnesty says Li Qiaochu was punished after publicly describing torture inflicted on her partner and the ill-treatment she faced in detention. That is evidence of retaliation against exposure of state abuse, not protection from it. | `3B.1` |
| Strong negative | `China: Free Jailed Tiananmen Participants, Supporters, and Advocates for Justice` | Chinese Human Rights Defenders | 2024-05-31 | https://www.nchrd.org/2024/05/china-free-jailed-tiananmen-participants-supporters-and-advocates-for-justice/ | CHRD said 27 Tiananmen participants/supporters/advocates were still in detention or prison in 2024 and that Beijing had spent decades erasing June 4 through persecution. This supports the political-imprisonment and arbitrary-punishment side of the lens. | `3B.1` |

**Synthesis**
- Best-supported conclusion: **No**, Xi did not protect residents from state violence in a meaningful general sense in 2024.
- The positive evidence is narrow and mostly procedural: one Tibet finding of no known arbitrary killings, and limited bail/acquittal outcomes in Hong Kong.
- The negative evidence is broad and direct: credible reports of torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, arbitrary detention, and impunity across Xinjiang, Tibet, Hong Kong, and mainland China.
- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Xi personally accepted responsibility for these abuses or that his system imposed credible accountability on the officials involved.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a credible 2024 source showing Xi ordered or tolerated a meaningful nationwide restraint mechanism against torture, disappearances, or political imprisonment.
- I also did not find strong evidence of top-level accountability for state abuse; the record is dominated by repression and selective, limited due-process exceptions.
